title: How a tropical storm forms
html: Sea above 27°Cwarms the air and fills it with moisture Warm, moist air risescools, condenses: tall cloud, heat given out Low pressure belowair rushes in to replace the rising air The Earth's spin turns itCoriolis effect: anticlockwise in the north The eyecalm, sinking air; the strongest winds round it

title: The greenhouse effect
html: Sunlight inshort-wave radiation passes through the air Heat outthe warm ground gives off long-wave radiation Greenhouse gases trap someand send it back: warm enough for life More gas from peoplefossil fuels, cattle, cutting down forests Enhanced greenhouse effectmore heat is trapped, so the Earth warms

title: Erosion and longshore drift
html: Hydraulic powerwaves force air into cracks; the pressure breaks the rock Abrasionpebbles hurled by the waves wear the cliff away A notch, then collapsethe overhang falls and the cliff retreats Swash up at an anglethe prevailing wind drives waves up the beach Longshore driftbackwash runs straight down, so pebbles move along

title: From meander to ox-bow lake
html: A gentle bendthe fastest flow swings to the outside The bend growserosion outside: river cliff; deposition inside: slip-off slope A narrow neckthe two outsides erode towards each other A flood cuts throughthe river takes the shortest course Ox-bow lakedeposition seals off the old bend

title: The water cycle and lag time
html: Evaporationthe sun heats the sea; water vapour rises Condensationthe vapour cools into cloud over the hills Precipitationrain falls on the drainage basin To the riverfast over the ground, slowly through the soil The storm hydrographrain as bars, the river's discharge as a line Lag timefrom peak rainfall to peak discharge

title: The demographic transition model
